evidence: paper: \Delta w_m = \mathrm{curl}_*\!\left(\frac{\mathrm{i}\,n_\Phi \times (\psi t_m)}{km\,|n_\Phi|^2}\, e^{ikm\Phi}\right), \qquad \Delta p_{w,m} = \psi \pi_m e^{ikm\Phi}, \qquad \mathscr{L}_m(t_m,\pi_m) = -f_m.

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. All three formulas are present, each up to a stated encoding. (i) The potential: Lean's `vectorPotential K R Vr Vθ Vz Φ a` is vectorMode K Φ applied to (i/K)·(n_Φ × a)/|n_Φ|², i.e. literally i n_Φ × a /(K|n_Φ|²) e^{iKΦ} with K = km and a = ψt_m (the ψ supplied by `withCutoff`, which multiplies amplitude and pressure by the same ψ, matching ψt_m and ψπ_m). Δw_m is its curl_*, which is `cylindricalCurl` (the cylindrical curl including the frame-connection term in its axial component). (ii) `cylindricalCurl_vectorPotential` states that this curl equals vectorMode K Φ (realizedCoefficient) = (a + curlRemainder) e^{iKΦ}, i.e. the realized amplitude is ψt_m plus the O(1/km) curl remainder; the paper's display itself only defines Δw_m as the curl, so this is a match, but note Lean makes the remainder explicit at this point whereas the paper's display does not name it. Lean's theorem also carries two hypotheses the display leaves implicit: n_Φ ≠ 0 on the chart, and the tangency normalDot n_Φ (a x) = 0. (iii) Δp_{w,m} = ψπ_m e^{ikmΦ}: the ψπ_m coefficient is `withCutoff`'s pressure field and the e^{ikmΦ} realization is `HarmonicBlock.oscillatoryPressure`, which takes the real part of HarmonicFields.field and carries an extra angular factor e^{i j kp θ} — a real-part/conjugate-pair encoding of the paper's complex display, consistent with the paper's own next sentence about retaining conjugate pairs. (iv) ℒ_m(t_m,π_m) = -f_m is stated as `complexCopyCoefficients_principal_at`, with ℒ_m = `LinearWaveResidual.principal` matching (9.1) term for term: transport along V_f, the shear matrix K, the εκ²|n_Φ|² damping and the ik n_Φ π pressure term. No constant, sign or exponent differs.
